page: Microsoft Azure D8nls_v6 is a network-optimized, reduced-memory virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. Hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs backed by 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The underlying processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

The instance provides 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio corresponding to 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring managed remote volumes for persistent disk storage, with support for Premium Storage tiers. No discrete GPU acceleration hardware is present. The reduced memory allocation per execution thread positions the instance as a cost-efficient deployment option for workloads that do not require standard memory densities.

Empirical benchmark testing places the instance within median cloud performance tiers, recording a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 7031.14 and a PassMark CPU rating of 12481.2. Memory operations achieve 63.58 GB/s in large-block uncached sequential reads and 43.81 GB/s in writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate throughput of 13.36 GB/s for static web serving and 9.63 million Redis SET operations per second. Given the limited RAM capacity and dedicated compute cores, the D8nls_v6 is suited for network routing appliances, reverse proxies, distributed build pipelines, and stateless web microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D8nls_v6 is an Intel-powered virtual machine tailored for compute-driven tasks that require minimal memory capacity and elevated network efficiency. Operating on 8 dedicated vCPUs from a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor across 4 physical cores, the instance includes 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a constrained 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and provides no local storage, requiring attached network disks for file operations. Benchmarking shows steady mid-tier execution with a PassMark CPU score of 12481.2, 9.63 million Redis SET operations per second, and 13.36 GB/s static web serving throughput. With its low memory overhead and dedicated execution units, the D8nls_v6 fits network appliances, front-end microservices, distributed CI/CD pipelines, and lightweight computational batch jobs.
